question.problem:
At a particular helpdesk, customer waiting times occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of $6$ customers per hour. If a customer has already waited for $6$ minutes, what is the probability that they will need to wait at least $4$ more minutes for their call to be answered? Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

The required probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since waiting times occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next call is answered using an exponential distribution.

Let $X$ be the customer's waiting time, in minutes. Since the help desk serves $6$ customers per hour on average (or $1$ customer every $10$ minutes), the rate is $\lambda =\frac{1}{10}$ customers per minute, and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{10}).
$$

Recall that exponential random variables have the memoryless property. So, given two positive real numbers $s,t,$ we have that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =\frac{1}{10},$ $s=6,$ and $t=4.$ 

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6+4\,|\,X>6) & =P(X>4) \\  & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(1/10)\cdot (4)} \\  & ={e}^{-2/5} \\  & ≈0.670.\end{aligned}
$$
